title: Continuous Subarray Sum
description:
Given an integer array `nums` and a positive integer `k`, return `true` if `nums` has a **good subarray**, or `false` otherwise.

A **good subarray** is a contiguous subarray where:
- Its length is **at least two**, and
- The sum of the elements of the subarray is a **multiple of `k`**.

Note that an integer `x` is a multiple of `k` if there exists an integer `n` such that `x = n * k`. In particular, `0` is always a multiple of `k`.
hints: Two prefix sums `prefix[j]` and `prefix[i]` have a difference divisible by `k` if and only if they share the same remainder modulo `k`.
Store the earliest index where each remainder `prefix % k` appears in a hash map, seeded with `{0: -1}`.
Only return `true` when the same remainder is seen again at an index `j` with `j - firstIndex[rem] >= 2`, and never overwrite an earlier index.

examples.explanation: [2, 4] is a contiguous subarray of size 2 whose elements sum up to 6, which is a multiple of 6.
[23, 2, 6, 4, 7] is a contiguous subarray of size 5 whose elements sum up to 42 = 7 * 6.
No contiguous subarray of length at least 2 has a sum divisible by 13.
